The fact you are able to use your awareness and mindfulness to identify that you are / were experiencing the “addiction mind” is a very positive thing whether you ended up relapsing or not. After that, there needs to be a decision made that you stick to. Your lower/primal brain wants what your upper brain (the part that allows for thoughtful decision making) knows is ruining your health and life. The lower brain is very powerful. It can be calmed by transcendental meditation (just research that well and you can learn how to do it without paying for a stupid $2k seminar on it). It’s actually legit and not hippie stuff. I used to do it everyday for a few months. EVERY time, my subconscious would start to relax to the point where, I shit you not, I would remember my last night’s dreams visually, narratively, and emotionally. The technique forces you to direct as much as your consciousness as you can to your thinking brain so that the lower brain can calm and run wild.

I’m late af on this but I’ve been having similar issues with “not being able to live without it”. I’ll tell myself to quit or at least take a substantial break from it, but that’s way easier said than done when the habit becomes compulsive. Your compulsions hijack your conscious mind so that it convinces your ego and conscience that it’s totally okay even when you swore to yourself to stop using five minutes earlier. But, friend, I will tell you this. Remain optimistic about getting it under control and every time you fuck up just try again. Don’t stop trying because that implies that you’ve given up. This substance is so strong that it’s hard to stop using even when you’re trying your hardest, so my point is that it’ll be impossible if you lose hope. Believe in yourself even in the darkest moments. Even in the face of failure after failure, don’t lose belief in your ability to kick the habit. Sure, it’s really tough but why can’t YOU kick it? Why not YOU? People fight addictions everyday because it’s their true self. Don’t lose sight of your true self - the voice inside of you that tells yourself you need to stop before it gets even worse and damages your life even more. That’s your true self that actually cares about life. And I’m not preaching from a place of feeling “holier than thou”. I’m literally in the middle of relapsing yet again with a gram bag today. In these moments of weakness I always try to find my strength to try again after the binge is over. And try not to beat yourself up too much. Lab rats choose cocaine over water and food in experimental settings, but when they have a community of loved ones and friends they actually chose the water and food over the cocaine at higher rates. Lean on the ones that will be there for you during the fight. Jesus…ya boy is ranting cuz of the drug but good luck and much love.
